key_insight: A reinforcement-learning policy can decide when to reuse source-domain knowledge and when to rely on target data, reducing negative transfer for carbon-footprint prediction in new manufacturing domains.
engineering_relevance: This enables more reliable early-stage embodied-carbon estimates for new materials and processes in additive manufacturing, supporting faster design and sustainability decisions with limited target data.
method: Trains a selective transfer policy that compares source-based predictors against supervised alternatives.
Uses a validation gate to accept transferred predictions only when they outperform target-only or fully pooled models.
Applied to embodied GHG prediction for material-extrusion AM using 22 material, process, and toolpath features.
evidence_signal: On 729 experiments across five materials, leave-one-material-out testing achieved a mean RMSE of 5.2 g CO2e per part, outperforming target-only training by 20.00% and source-target pooling by 10.30%.
watch_item: Performance depends on having enough representative source domains and a reliable validation split; poorly matched source data can still limit transfer if the gating policy is not well calibrated.
paper_title: Learning When to Transfer: Reinforcement Learning for Carbon-Footprint Modeling in New Manufacturing Domains
